title: API change tolerance and rollout decision matrix for serving runtime
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: define a pragmatic semantic-versioning policy for the serving runtime that reduces customer surprise while enabling necessary internal refactors. This ticket codifies a change-tolerance classification, rollout decision matrix, deprecation windows, LTS channel expectations, and required upgrade-tooling outputs for consumers and internal operators. Key outcomes: (1) a 4-tier change tolerance taxonomy (Tier 0: Emergency breaking fixes only; Tier 1: Strict compatibility; Tier 2: Negotiable compatibility with adapter; Tier 3: Extension-only nonbreaking) with clear accepted examples for each; (2) deprecation windows tied to stability tiers and LTS channels (minor deprecations get 6 months + 2 LTS releases; breaking changes require formal migration assistant and 12 month notice where possible); (3) rollout gates: canary -> regional canary -> global gradual rollout with automated health gate checks (latency, error-rate, model-compat regressions, API contract violations); (4) upgrade-tooling requirements: changes that affect wire format must publish an automated adapter generator run and a machine-readable migration plan; (5) client negotiation header: runtime will support an Accept-Runtime-Version and X-Runtime-Compat header that allows clients to opt-in to new behaviors or request strict compat; (6) telemetry: changes must include compatibility impact tests and a consumer-impact score derived from production telemetry sampling. The doc also prescribes operator rollback criteria and a short-run mitigation playbook for immediate incompatibility regressions.
